answer: A newcomer earns standing by firing quartz glass, glazing each piece with a pigment they made and logging each firing — temperature curve, pigment recipe, and a sonnet recounting it, witnessed by a neighbour. Two kiln masters verify the log within five days, checking curve against known profile and recipe against the piece. A copied sonnet, a curve the kiln could not produce, or a missing firing voids the season, burns the 50-credit stake and bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 50 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 stakes and 1,000 seasons of sonnets, each checked at a kiln.
